headline: Computational tools mining mutational and transcriptomic patterns in cancer genomes
label: Computational Cancer Genomic Profiling
summary: Recent releases pair transcriptome-based leukemia subtyping with WGS/WES-only mutation recurrence and Bayesian signature inference across about 8000 samples.
synthesis: The common thread is computational inference of molecular structure from large genomic datasets. TASC is a transcriptome-based machine learning classifier that predicts multi-omic T-ALL subtypes across patient samples and cell lines, with the stated aim of exploring molecular heterogeneity and relapse-associated programs. DORM is a web database of recurrent cancer mutations built only from whole-genome and whole-exome data, excluding targeted panels and duplicates. BASCULE applies Bayesian inference with biological priors to expand mutational signature catalogues and group patients by shared signature patterns, applied to about 8000 samples. What is new across these items is methodological: subtype and signature assignment derived directly from transcriptomic or sequencing data at scale, with resources that aggregate recurrence information from whole-genome and whole-exome sources.
